title: Germany Advances Key Consortia in €640 Million ($717.2 Million USD) Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Competition
key_facts: Germany's Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) advanced six industrial and academic consortia through the outline phase of its Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing With Pilot Line Development competition.

The competition allocates up to €640 million ($717.2 million) in national funding, under the High-Tech Agenda Deutschland, to deploy at least two fault-tolerant quantum processing units (QPUs) by 2030.
Three hardware platforms are assessed (neutral atoms, trapped ions, superconducting circuits), with two consortia per platform selected to submit full proposals.
Selected consortia must demonstrate functioning entry systems by 31 Mar 2027 before advancing toward the 2030 goals.
Neutral atoms: Munich start-up planqc leads the LOGIQC consortium (ytterbium atom arrays plus pilot-line optical and laser infrastructure), rooted in Munich Quantum Valley.

Trapped ions: AQT Germany GmbH and Quantum Valley Lower Saxony partners (Leibniz University Hannover, TU Braunschweig, PTB) detail their roles in the €122 million (about $138.8 million) NFQC-1k project, a 1,000-qubit system.
QCR points to its earlier coverage of the QUDORA-led NFQC-1k announcement (QCR listing dated 24 Sep 2026).
quote_evidence: The national competition evaluates the three most mature hardware platforms—neutral atoms, trapped ions, and superconducting circuits—with two consortia selected per technology stream to submit full proposals.
Selected consortia must demonstrate functioning entry systems by March 31, 2027, before advancing toward 2030 fault-tolerant scaling goals.

In the neutral-atom category, Munich-based startup planqc leads the LOGIQC (Logical Operations, Gates and Infrastructure for Quantum Computing) consortium, originating from the Munich Quantum Valley (MQV).
why_it_matters_hint: Shows which German teams stay in line for state money to build error-correcting quantum computers by 2030.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 for the six-consortia list and planqc's selection; the QUDORA-led trapped-ion project was reported on 24 Sep 2026.
